newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end lower on blue chip selling.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end lower on blue chip selling.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended lower on Thursday as the index was dragged down as the selling in blue chip stocks was led by a sharp fall in Telkom, brokers said.
"Sustained selling in Indosat, Indocement and Indofood had put pressure on the index since the morning, but then the sharp fall of Telkom pushed it down even further," a broker with foreign firm.
The Jakarta Composite Index was down 3.09 points, or 0.43 percent, to close at 709.41 points. Gainers led losers by 68 to 64, with 67 counters unchanged. Total turn-over was about 736 billion rupiah.
"This (the fall in the index) is due to profit-taking as the market is still in a period of consolidation," Adnan Tan, sales director of Morgan Grenfell Asia Indonesia, said.

"Most of the profit-taking has been done this week and tomorrow I expect profit-taking as well. Next week I expect the index to continue drift down due to the three days of holidays in Hongkong for the hand-over," Tan said.

But Tan said the fund inflow to Indonesia was still positive and brokers were net buyers."The support level is definitely there. The market is very healthy, there's nothing to be afraid of," he added.
Brokers said the sharp fall in blue chips Telkom and Indosat could be due to profit-taking.
Property firm Bakrieland Development was the most active stock with about 49 million shares traded, rising 175 rupiah to 1,950 rupiah on speculative interest, brokers said.
"The report that its right issue plan will be finalised soon has sparked further speculation of the price and what companies they are going to acquire," one local broker said.

Eddy Sobari, vice president of Bakrie Capital Indonesia -- which owns a 70 percent controlling stake in Bakrieland Development -- said the company was planning to finalise details of a planned rights issue next month.

"I hope the rights issue will be effective sometime in August. We are going to submit the proposal to Bapepam (the Capital Markets Supervisory Body) next month," Sobari told Reuters, but he declined to give any further details.
Sobari also said the proceeds would be used to finance some acquisitions. But no details were available.
Strong sentiment in Bakrieland had lifted sentiment on another property firm Surya Semesta which also due to speculative interest, brokers said.

"Large buying in Surya Semesta is linked to revived market talk that its plan to link-up with Australian company to build cargo terminal in its industrial park is in the final stage," one broker said.
Surya was last traded at 1,225 rupiah, or 100 rupiah higher on a volume of 23.5 million shares.
